External Services and APIs

This plugin integrates with the following external third-party services. Please review this section carefully to understand what data is transmitted and to whom.

IMPORTANT: All external API calls are made server-side using WordPress’s native wp_remote_post() and wp_remote_get() functions. API keys are stored securely in your WordPress database and are never exposed to the frontend.

AI Services (Require API Keys)

1. OpenAI API
– Service Provider: OpenAI, LLC (api.openai.com)
– What it’s used for: Content generation using ChatGPT, GPT-4, and GPT-4o models, as well as DALL-E image generation.
– Data transmitted: When you use AI content generation features, the following data is sent to OpenAI:
* Your API key (for authentication)
* Content prompts/text you provide
* Model preferences and generation parameters (temperature, max tokens, etc.)
* Your website domain (for API usage tracking)
– When data is sent: Data is transmitted only when you actively use AI content generation features (creating posts, generating images, etc.). No data is sent automatically in the background.
– Terms of Service: https://openai.com/api/policies/terms/
– Privacy Policy: https://openai.com/api/policies/privacy/

2. Google Gemini API
– Service Provider: Google LLC (generativelanguage.googleapis.com)
– What it’s used for: Content generation using Google’s Gemini Pro and other Gemini models.
– Data transmitted: When you use Gemini-powered features, the following data is sent to Google:
* Your API key (for authentication)
* Content prompts/text you provide
* Model preferences and generation parameters
* Your website domain (for API usage tracking)
– When data is sent: Data is transmitted only when you actively use Gemini content generation features. No data is sent automatically in the background.
– Terms of Service: https://ai.google.dev/terms
– Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

3. Cloudflare Workers AI
– Service Provider: Cloudflare, Inc. (api.cloudflare.com)
– What it’s used for: AI-powered image generation using Stable Diffusion and other AI models hosted on Cloudflare’s infrastructure.
– Data transmitted: When you use Cloudflare AI image generation, the following data is sent to Cloudflare:
* Your API token (for authentication)
* Your Cloudflare account ID
* Image generation prompts/descriptions you provide
* Model selection preferences
– When data is sent: Data is transmitted only when you actively use the Cloudflare AI image generation feature. No data is sent automatically in the background.
– Terms of Service: https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/
– Privacy Policy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacy/

4. Hugging Face API
– Service Provider: Hugging Face, Inc. (api-inference.huggingface.co)
– What it’s used for: AI image generation using Hugging Face’s hosted AI models.
– Data transmitted: When you use Hugging Face image generation, the following data is sent to Hugging Face:
* Your API token (for authentication)
* Image generation prompts/descriptions you provide
* Model selection preferences
– When data is sent: Data is transmitted only when you actively use the Hugging Face image generation feature. No data is sent automatically in the background.
– Terms of Service: https://huggingface.co/terms-of-use
– Privacy Policy: https://huggingface.co/privacy

5. AI Auto Tool Service (bard.aitoolseo.com)
– Service Provider: AI Auto Tool (bard.aitoolseo.com)
– What it’s used for: Free alternative AI content generation service when API keys are not configured. This service provides content rewriting, full article generation, and image search functionality.
– Data transmitted: When you use the free AI service (when no API keys are configured), the following data is sent to bard.aitoolseo.com:
* Content prompts/text you provide
* Language preferences
* Your website domain
* Plugin information (for service management)
– When data is sent: Data is transmitted only when you actively use AI content generation features without configured API keys. This service is optional and only used if you choose not to configure your own API keys.
– Terms of Service: https://aiautotool.com/terms
– Privacy Policy: https://aiautotool.com/privacy

Google Services (Require API Keys or Service Accounts)

6. Google Custom Search API
– Service Provider: Google LLC (www.googleapis.com/customsearch)
– What it’s used for: Web search functionality to find relevant content, images, and information for your articles.
– Data transmitted: When you use the web search feature, the following data is sent to Google:
* Your API key (for authentication)
* Your Custom Search Engine ID (CX)
* Search queries you enter
* Number of results requested
* Language preferences
– When data is sent: Data is transmitted only when you actively use the web search feature within the plugin. No data is sent automatically in the background.
– Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/custom-search/terms
– Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

7. Google Indexing API
– Service Provider: Google LLC (indexing.googleapis.com)
– What it’s used for: Submitting URLs to Google Search Console for faster indexing of your published content.
– Data transmitted: When you use the URL indexing feature, the following data is sent to Google:
* Your Service Account JSON credentials (for authentication)
* URLs of posts/pages you want to index
* Request type (URL_UPDATED or URL_DELETED)
– When data is sent: Data is transmitted only when you actively submit URLs for indexing through the plugin’s indexing feature. No data is sent automatically in the background.
– Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/search/apis/indexing-api/v3/quota-pricing
– Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Embedded Services (No API Key Required)

8. Google AMP Stories (CDN)
– Service Provider: Google LLC (cdn.ampproject.org)
– What it’s used for: The plugin embeds AMP (Accelerated Mobile Pages) scripts from Google’s CDN to create AMP-compliant Web Stories. This is similar to embedding YouTube videos or Twitter feeds – the scripts are required for the service to function properly.
– Data transmitted: When visitors view Web Stories pages, their browsers automatically load AMP scripts from Google’s CDN. This is standard browser behavior for loading external JavaScript resources. The plugin itself does not send any data to Google for this service.
– When data is sent: AMP scripts are loaded by visitors’ browsers when they access Web Stories pages. This is client-side loading and does not involve server-side data transmission from your WordPress site.
– Terms of Service: https://amp.dev/about/terms/
– Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

sections.faq:
Is a Gemini Pro account required for all features?

No need to enter API KEY Gemini pro. you just need to install and use. Extremely easy without needing an API KEY

Do I need SEO knowledge to use the plugin effectively?

A: While not mandatory, having SEO knowledge will help you maximize the plugin’s potential for website optimization.

Can I use the plugin in languages other than English?

Absolutely! The plugin supports multiple languages for both writing assistance and content generation.

How can I secure my content from unauthorized copying?

The plugin includes a content security feature to prevent unauthorized copying and ensure the protection of your valuable content.
